subject.title: Support Slack user-level events (events on behalf of users) for DM routing

question: Should OpenClaw support a Slack user-account DM mode that receives events and replies as a regular Slack user, and what authorization, scope, and audit boundaries must that mode enforce?
rationale: The missing code path is clear, but automation should not decide whether OpenClaw may impersonate a Slack user identity or how to map Slack event authorizations to stored xoxp credentials.

options.title: Explicit user-account DM mode
options.body: Add a named Slack plugin mode with user-event subscriptions, authorization-to-token routing, user-token replies, docs, tests, and live Slack proof while leaving bot mode as the default.

options.title: Keep bot-only inbound support
options.body: Document that OpenClaw supports bot/app DMs and user-token read helpers but does not receive or reply as regular Slack users.

options.title: Defer to external plugin/router
options.body: Keep core Slack behavior unchanged until a separate router or plugin API proves a safe user-identity integration boundary.

recommendation.title: Explicit user-account DM mode
recommendation.body: Add a named Slack plugin mode with user-event subscriptions, authorization-to-token routing, user-token replies, docs, tests, and live Slack proof while leaving bot mode as the default.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest visible combination of merged user-token context, recent Slack/plugin-boundary history, and current-main provenance around the affected files.
